question: When is the National Unity Day celebrated in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fri Oct 31 2025 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Unity Day, also known as **Rashtriya Ekta Diwas**, is celebrated in India on **October 31** every year.
 
• This day commemorates the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who played a key role in the unification of India.
 
• It was introduced by the Government of India in **2014** to honor Sardar Patel's contributions to national integration.
 
• Various events such as the **"Run for Unity"** are organized across the country to mark this occasion.
 
• The day emphasizes the importance of maintaining the country's unity and integrity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

 
 
• Also known as the **"Iron Man of India"**.
 
• First Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
 
• Played a crucial role in the integration of over 500 princely states into the Indian Union.
 
• His efforts and strategies were pivotal in maintaining the nation's unity post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Statue of Unity**
 
 
• Located in the state of Gujarat, India.
 
• It is the world's tallest statue, standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet).
 
• Dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and inaugurated on October 31, 2018.
 
• Symbolizes Patel's vision of a united India.
 
 
 
• **Run for Unity**
 
 
• An annual event organized on National Unity Day.
 
• Aims to promote national integration and communal harmony.
 
• Participants from various walks of life join to reinforce the message of unity.
 
 
 
• **National Unity Day Pledge**
 
 
• People take a pledge to preserve the unity, integrity, and security of the nation.
 
• Emphasizes the importance of working towards a stronger and more unified India.
 
• Often recited in schools, colleges, and government offices on this day.
